title: SSO/SAML session management: JIT provisioning, MFA posture, logout & re-auth policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement SSO/SAML session management improvements focused on: (1) Just-In-Time (JIT) provisioning durability and session binding, (2) clearly defined MFA expectations and enforcement model for IdP vs. Redwood, (3) reliable SP-initiated and IdP-initiated logout mechanics plus forced session termination for deprovisioning, and (4) re-authentication policies for high-risk operations. Deliverables include API hooks, Console UI for active sessions and force-logout, comprehensive audit events, and an ops playbook for incidents involving SSO sessions.
acceptance_criteria: JIT-provisioned users receive a stable Redwood user id and a server-side session tied to the SAML assertion session index where supported
MFA posture is represented in the user's session metadata and respected for re-auth flows (e.g., privileged workflows require recent MFA), with clear policy default and override rules
SP-initiated and IdP-initiated logout flows terminate the corresponding Redwood session and emit audit events within 10s under normal load
Admin can list and terminate active sessions for a user in Console and via API; forced termination blocks future token refreshes
Audit log contains structured events for SSO login, MFA assertion, logout, session revoke, and deprovision-triggered termination and is searchable in Console (30d retention for rollout)
implementation_notes: Create session record fields: saml_session_index, idp_issuer, last_mfa_timestamp, session_ttl_seconds, session_state (active/revoked/expired)
When IdP provides SessionIndex, persist it and use it to map IdP-initiated logouts to Redwood sessions; fallback to hashed assertion ID when absent
MFA expectation model: accept 'enforced-by-idp' and 'recommended-by-idp' flags from SAML attributes; default policy is to treat absent MFA as 'unknown' and require re-auth for sensitive routes
Expose API endpoint POST /admin/sessions/terminate that accepts user_id or session_id; termination must cascade to revoke refresh tokens and in-memory caches
Add rate-limited background job to poll SAML Single Logout (SLO) endpoints for IdPs that support asynchronous logout hooks
Design trade-off: we will not attempt universal cross-IdP session introspection; rely on session index + IdP-initiated hooks + provisioning events for coverage to avoid brittle polling
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Instrument session metadata and audit events behind feature flag for 5% of SSO customers; no UI changes
Phase 2 (beta): Enable admin list & terminate UI in Console for pilot customers and internal orgs; expand audit retention to 30d
Phase 3 (general): Default feature flag on for all SSO customers, expose API for session termination, and add re-auth prompts to sensitive endpoints
Fallback: If SLO accuracy <95% during canary, fallback to stored sessions + customer notif rather than automatic termination
testing_plan: Unit tests for session lifecycle transitions (create, bind to SAML assertion, refresh, revoke)
Integration tests with test SAML IdP (SSO test harness) covering: JIT provisioning, SP and IdP logout, missing SessionIndex behavior
E2E tests simulating deprovision event: user removed in IdP triggers immediate session termination and audit event
Load test measuring logout latency and audit event emission at target throughput (baseline: 1000 logins/min)
audit_events_to_log: sso.login.success: includes user_id, idp_issuer, saml_assertion_id, saml_session_index, mfa_present
admin_controls: Console: 'Active sessions' pane on User page showing device, last_seen, idp_issuer, saml_session_index, MFA age; action: 'Terminate session'
Org policy toggles: require_mfa_for_admin_actions (on/off), max_session_age_days, require_reauth_for_sensitive_scopes
Audit-only mode: admins can enable 'audit-only' to observe SLOs without automatic termination during initial rollout
privacy_considerations: Persist only minimal SAML attributes required for session binding (avoid storing full assertions), redact PII from logs by default
Add configuration to stop storing raw IdP responses for customers with strict data residency requirements
Document data retention in Console and honor org-level retention overrides
security_considerations: Protect session termination API with RBAC v2 check: only users with 'session.admin' role can terminate other users' sessions
Throttle termination calls to prevent abuse; record initiator in audit events
Ensure session revocation invalidates in-memory KV caches across runtime nodes (publish invalidate message to runtime control plane)
comments: 2026-02-20 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created. Captured scope after discussion with PM and Security. Key asks: reliable logout, admin force-logout, MFA posture.
2026-02-25 - Marcus Li: Spike completed for persisting saml_session_index and mapping IdP-initiated logout requests. Found IdPs in pilot do not always include SessionIndex; added fallback plan.
2026-03-02 - Security Review (Nisha Rao): Requested explicit RBAC check for termination endpoint and logging of termination initiator. Also asked for default policy when IdP omits MFA claim.
2026-03-05 - UX (Jordi Alvarez): Mockups for Active Sessions pane reviewed. Suggested showing 'MFA verified X minutes ago' and confirmation modal when admin terminates session.

2026-03-08 - Marcus Li: Implemented backend session model and audit event schema. Added feature flag 'sso_session_v2' and created alpha DB migration script. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4123
2026-03-10 - QA (Samira Khan): Integration tests added to SSO harness. Found race where deprovision event and IdP-initiated logout can both attempt termination — added idempotency guard.
notes_on_tradeoffs: We considered full outbound SAML Logout requests to IdPs for every admin-initiated termination, but rejected due to inconsistent SLO behavior across vendors and potential latency; instead we will rely on local session revoke + optional outbound SLO for IdPs that opt-in

We could enforce MFA at Redwood by challenging users directly, but to avoid duplicating IdP functionality and to support enterprise SSO posture, default is to honor IdP-provided MFA claims and require re-auth only when claim absent or stale
